content.rendered: Might be since you applied 9/1 so are subject to the old (more lenient) policy
The whole point of the post is that N/24 may vary with the other factors

No it isn’t.

N/24 does not “vary with other factors”.

N/24 is the number of CCs <24 months old visible on the personal credit report pulled. If you don’t keep the other factors separate you haven’t counted your n/24 and it’s not a valid DP.

The reason for the post is Chase seems to have introduced a lower limit for sole props. I.e., the new upper limit might be 2/24 instead of 4/24. Maybe the new limit is a soft limit.

There are other factors like number of open biz cards. Those are soft rules and they are independent of the hard 5/24 rule.

Maybe 3/24 is a soft rule, or temporary.

if 3/24 includes only chase business cards, I might be able to get down to 2/24 with judicious use of non-chase business cards. It will be harder than 4/24, but possible. Depending on the chase card im interested in I may need to just pause for awhile. overall probably need to slow down, set my own x/24 limit so its possible to see 2/24 again.

I’m here to add another unsuccessful dp.
Background:
Sp, 3/24 plus a CIP opened 5 months ago. I got a ‘youre already approved (not pre-approved)’ pop up on the app, and ‘youre pre-approved ‘ email a few weeks ago.  After this new 3/24 for sp dp started circulating, I applied for CIC a couple of weeks ago.  

The link for application in the app kept saying ‘it looks like this isn’t working right now’. I called in, the rep refused to accept my application over the phone. I went to their web page, logged in, then submitted my app. Instant rejection, telling me I’d receive more information in a letter in 7-10 days.  

The following day, I received an email telling me that I got a secure message in the app. The letter there said that they couldn’t approve me for a number of opened accounts.  

I called recon today, I was told about 3/24, the rep refused to move existing credit limit from my CIP for the new card. I realized that I forgot to ask him about ‘youre already approved ‘ pop up, so I called again. The next rep told me the same thing, and she clarified that pop-up in the app was just a pre approval (doesn’t mean much), and there’s always a complete assessment after application. I asked her about the possibility of moving existing cl to a new card, she transferred me to an underwriter. The underwriter refused it as well.

I regret that I didn’t apply soon as I got that pop up, but hindsight is always 20/20. Now I rarely stay under 3/24, so I guess Chase business cards will be out of reach for me for a long time.

Last month I had applied for my first Ink card not knowing that 5/24 lasts through the calendar month. I had called reconsideration this morning (10/1) and they said they were still unable to approve me. So at this point I’m 4/24 and rejected.

Applied for Chase Sapphire Business Reserve on 9/29, denied 9/30 for too many accounts (I’m 4/24) and called recon on 10/1. Front line rep claimed 3/24 is the limit and I asked to speak to an underwriter. Underwriter confirmed the policy changed 9/16 and it is 3/24. I did not ask if it was only applicable to sole props, but I am a sole prop.

Called recon today for Business Reserve after denial last month. I was at 4 personal and 1 Chase Business card in the last 24 months. 2 of the personal cards were opened 10/2024. They approved me after seeing 4 cards with 2 hitting the 2 year mark.

Implies Chase Biz cards not counted against 3/24 like some say.

One TBD is whether P2s 40K referral bonus will post. I closed my Hyatt Biz in August and that left me with 0 Chase Business Cards. Am I considered a “new” business customer for purposes of the bonus? Don’t see T&Cs specifying how they define “new” here.
